title: Quantization of cyclic invariant charges of the closed string
statement: Construct and describe an associative formal quantum deformation of the Poisson algebra of cyclic iterated integrals of closed-string chiral currents, with prescribed classical bracket.
status: As of November 2026, abstract existence follows from quasi-Lie-bialgebra quantization, with the string application stated by Bahns--Meinecke. Naive canonical normal ordering fails. A preferred explicit presentation or positive representation is a stronger target than the recorded existence question.

title: Global free energy of the recorded four-unitary matrix integral
statement:
For four independent probability-Haar matrices in \(U(N)\), set \[Z_N( eta)=\mathbb E\exp\!\left[- eta N\sum_{\mu,
u=1}^4\operatorname{tr}(U_\mu U_
u U_\mu^\dagger U_
u^\dagger)ight].\] Determine the existence and value of \(F( eta)=\lim_{N	o\infty}N^{-2}\log Z_N( eta)\) for all real \( eta\), including analytic branches and transition values. The full ordered sum and negative exponent are retained.
status: As of November 2026, rigorous small-potential theory supplies a local analytic limit; the chapter computes \(F(\beta)=-4\beta+6\beta^2+O(\beta^3)\). The all-coupling formula and transition structure for this precise convention were not located. This is a bounded search conclusion, not a claim that no relevant unpublished solution exists.

title: Reducibility and first singular vectors of Virasoro Verma modules
statement: Determine all pairs \((h,c)\) for which the complex Virasoro Verma module is reducible, and the least positive level of a singular vector.
status: As of November 2026, solved before the September 1982 talk by the Kac determinant criterion, with a proof in Feigin--Fuchs (1982). Later appearances in this year reuse this identifier.

title: Recover a crossing value from hyperbola orbital integrals
statement: For compactly supported smooth \(f\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), recover \(f(0,0)\) from the family \(\int f(x,y)\delta(xy-c)\,dx\,dy\), \(c\ne0\).
status: As of November 2026, an elementary solved singular-asymptotic problem: the leading coefficient is \(-2f(0,0)\log|c|\). The notebook already refers to the older generalized-functions treatment.

title: Nonminimal finite-energy SU(2) Yang–Mills–Higgs critical points
statement: In the Prasad--Sommerfield limit on \(\mathbb R^3\), with \(|\Phi|\to v>0\), do finite-energy stationary points exist outside the Bogomolny minimum equations? A fixed magnetic-charge sector must be specified separately.
status: As of November 2026: existence was published in September 1982. Later sectorwise multiplicity is covered by Taubes with his 1989 correction. This Higgs-field problem on \(\mathbb R^3\) differs from the earlier pure four-dimensional Yang--Mills problem GP-1977-04.

title: Existence of a unit instanton when the second cohomology vanishes
statement: For every smooth metric on a closed oriented simply connected four-manifold with \(H^2(M;\mathbb R)=0\), does the \(SU(2)\) bundle of charge one admit an anti-self-dual connection?
status: As of November 2026: yes, by the Taubes result reported in 1982. Verification is indirect through Donaldson, Section 3, citing the exact Taubes theorem; the incorrect notebook journal/year is separately logged.

title: Asymptotic completeness for three quantum particles with Coulomb forces
statement: For three nonrelativistic quantum particles in \(\mathbb R^3\) with positive finite masses and pair Coulomb interactions, remove the center of mass. Do the Dollard-modified channel wave operators exhaust the continuous spectral subspace of the resulting Schrödinger Hamiltonian?
status: As of November 2026: established in Enss 1989, equations (1.12)--(1.13). The 1983 chapter is short-range and does not verify the Coulomb claim. Earlier 1971-252.3 is a thematic wave-operator discussion without an identical problem ID.

title: Primary correlators, conformal blocks and null-state equations
statement: Determine the constraints and calculational recursions for primary-field matrix elements from Virasoro covariance and specified null states, distinguishing the additional channel and three-point data needed to obtain a full correlation function.
status: As of November 2026, the BPZ program, received in November 1983 and published in 1984, gives conformal blocks and degenerate-field differential equations. The notebook data alone do not determine structure constants or a unique full conformal theory; this is an underdetermination, not a newly posed open classification problem.

title: The Virasoro representation content of the Liouville spectrum
statement: Relate the stationary spectrum of a quantized and renormalized Liouville field theory to highest-weight Virasoro representations. A precise modern version fixes \(0<\gamma<2\), \(\mu>0\), and the reflection-positive probabilistic Liouville Hamiltonian.
status: As of November 2026, the real-coupling implementation has a complete continuous spectral resolution with Virasoro descendant states, proved in the 2020 preprint of Guillarmou--Kupiainen--Rhodes--Vargas and published in 2024. This does not identify the unrenormalized notebook action at every \(D<26\) with that theorem.

title: Flag superspaces with reduced Grassmannian G(2,4)
statement: Classify classical homogeneous flag superspaces whose reduced manifold is \(G(2,4)\), with equivalence and flag-stabilizer convention specified.
status: As of November 2026: Manin’s 1983 chapter is the close publication match. Its complete classification has not been independently read; this entry does not assert that the question is still open.

title: Polyakov accessory-parameter conjecture
statement: For the complete hyperbolic metric on a sphere with distinct punctures, does a suitably regularized classical Liouville action generate the uniformizing accessory parameters under motion of the punctures?
status: As of November 2026: proved by Zograf and Takhtajan; 1985 announcement, 1987 Russian full paper, 1988 English translation. With their projective-connection normalization, \(c_i=-(2\pi)^{-1}\partial_{z_i}S\).

title: A p-adic analogue of the circle-diffeomorphism representations
statement: Construct a p-adic version of the almost-invariant-kernel and Fock/Gaussian construction of unitary diffeomorphism-group representations. The documented realization takes analytic diffeomorphisms of \(\mathbb P^1(\mathbb Q_p)\).
status: As of November 2026: Neretin’s 1984 construction solves the explicitly credited analytic-projective-line version \citep[introduction and Theorem 1]{neretin1984padic}. The group specification is supplied by that solution.

title: Geometric realization of compact-group weight multiplicities
statement: For an integral compact coadjoint orbit quantizing an irreducible representation, express its torus-weight multiplicities geometrically through the correctly normalized orbital character or the index of the corresponding reduced space, with the shifted quotient line bundle.
status: As of November 2026: finite-dimensional multiplicities are classical; the reduced-space index interpretation extends to singular reductions by \citet[Theorem 2.9 and Corollary 2.11]{meinrenkensjamaar1999singular} (July 1997 preprint; 1999 publication). A level set is not itself the reduced space, and reduced volume alone is not the finite-dimensional multiplicity.

title: Multiplicativity of zeta-regularized determinants
statement: For admissible elliptic operators, determine whether \(\det_\zeta(AB)=\det_\zeta A\det_\zeta B\), and if not identify its defect.
status: November 2026: false in general; local multiplicative-anomaly formulas solve the well-posed operator versions. See \citep{kontsevichvishik1994geometry,castillogarate2015anomaly}.

title: Classical modified Yang–Baxter operators on sl(2)
statement: Classify complex-linear \(R:\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\to\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\) with modified Yang--Baxter defect \(-[x,y]\), up to Lie-algebra automorphism.
status: November 2026: solved via the equivalent weight-one Rota--Baxter classification; no skew restriction may be silently imposed. See \citep{gubarevkozlov2023rota,semenov1983classical}.

title: Spectral zeta constructions without self-adjointness
statement: Extend complex-power, zeta and spectral-asymmetry constructions beyond self-adjoint elliptic operators under suitable spectral-cut hypotheses.
status: November 2026: complex powers and zeta functions are established for admissible elliptic operators; the cut must avoid principal-symbol spectrum as well as global spectrum. Boundary realizations need their own ellipticity conditions. See \citep{kontsevichvishik1994geometry,wodzicki1982spectral,seeley1968powers}.

title: Eta regularity without a bounding manifold
statement: Is the global eta function regular at zero for a self-adjoint elliptic operator without assuming it bounds an elliptic complex?
status: November 2026: yes for closed classical elliptic operators of positive order; APS III treats odd dimension and Gilkey 1981 supplies the general-dimensional result. Local residue densities need not vanish. See \citep{atiyahpatodisinger1976spectral3,gilkey1981residue}.

title: Global continuation of curve zeta functions
statement: For every smooth projective geometrically connected curve over \(\mathbb Q\), prove the expected meromorphic continuation and functional equation of its completed arithmetic zeta function, including the correct bad and archimedean factors.
status: November 2026: proved for genus one over \(\mathbb Q\) by modularity and for genus two over totally real fields by potential automorphy; open in unrestricted higher genus. See \citep{breuilconraddiamondtaylor2001modularity,boxercalegarigeepilloni2021surfaces,gee2026modularity}.

title: Automorphy of the H1 of arbitrary curves
statement: Associate suitable algebraic automorphic data to the compatible \(H^1\) Galois representations of arbitrary smooth projective curves over \(\mathbb Q\), matching local Euler factors and completions.
status: November 2026: general actual automorphy remains open. Potential automorphy is known for genus-two curves over totally real fields; the 2025 actual modularity theorem proves a specified residual-surjective ordinary genus-two class over \(\mathbb Q\). See \citep{boxercalegarigeepilloni2021surfaces,boxercalegarigeepilloni2025modularity,gee2026modularity}.
